tasks.title: Hide the console window when launching from the icon (windows_subsystem)
tasks.description: Launching the app from its icon opens a console window; closing that console kills the app because the exe is built as a console-subsystem binary. Add #![windows_subsystem = "windows"] to src-tauri/src/main.rs so Windows treats it as a GUI app.
tasks.details:
Symptom (John, Nov 10, 2026): he keeps killing the terminal window that opens when the app is started from its icon. Cause: src-tauri/src/main.rs has no windows_subsystem attribute, so the exe is a console-subsystem binary. When launched from Explorer/an icon, Windows creates a console window for it, and closing that console terminates the process (the app dies with it).

Fix: add `#![windows_subsystem = "windows"]` as the very first line of src-tauri/src/main.rs (a crate-level inner attribute; it must come before any item, including the //! doc comments). This marks the exe as a GUI (windows) subsystem binary, so Windows does not create a console window when it is launched from Explorer/an icon.

Side effect: println! output will not be visible when the app is run from a terminal. That is expected and fine for a GUI app; the app's own logs are unaffected.

Branch: ranger-no-console-window (off origin/main bac5a5c). No other files touched.
tasks.testStrategy: Rebuild with `cargo tauri build` on the ASUS (Windows); launch the app from its icon and confirm no console window appears. Verification caveat: the sandbox cannot compile the Tauri app (no GTK3) and cannot verify a Windows build — the ASUS rebuild is the real verification.
